reports.title: Indice des Prix à la Consommation (IPC)
reports.publisher: Institut National de la Statistique de Djibouti (INSTAD)
reports.description: UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF/G.23, sharper confirmation of instad.dj's site-wide inaccessibility): A direct curl fetch of https://instad.dj/IPCMAI2023.pdf (a URL that surfaced via web search under the title "Bulletin de l'Indice de Prix à la Consommation (IPC)" and looks like a direct PDF link) returned HTTP 200 with content-type text/html and only 4,309 bytes — it actually serves the Nuxt.js single-page-application shell (`<html data-capo=""><head>...<link rel="stylesheet" href="/_nuxt/entry.BrJGBI8s.css">`), not real PDF bytes. This confirms the failure is not limited to specific pages like /ipc.php or /indice/ipc — it is structural to the entire instad.dj domain, including URLs that look like static document links, none of which render server-side text to a non-JS-executing fetcher. Underlying conclusion unchanged: no independently-confirmable COICOP/methodology citation from INSTAD's own document. Djibouti's national CPI. INSTAD's institutional identity and existence are confirmed via its own founding decree (Décret n°2021-236/PR/MEFI, "Les statuts de l'Institut de la Statistique de Djibouti (INSTAD)... sont approuvés"), and the IMF's 2025 Article IV report (Country Report No. 25/276) reproduces CPI/inflation figures for Djibouti in its tables. HOWEVER: INSTAD's own live CPI pages (instad.dj/ipc.php) are JavaScript-rendered and returned no extractable text this round — base year, publication frequency, and any COICOP/IMF-Manual methodology citation could NOT be independently confirmed from INSTAD's own document this round. Secondary aggregators (TradingEconomics/FRED, mirroring World Bank data) suggest a "2005=100" rebasing, but this is a World Bank figure, not an INSTAD primary-document statement, so it is excluded per the branch's evidence standard. Flagged for a future session with rendering-capable browser access.

reports.title: Stratégie Nationale de Développement de la Statistique — Schéma Directeur de la Statistique 2011-2015
reports.description: Djibouti's national statistics development strategy (2011-2015 — an older document; a newer edition may exist and was not searched for this round). Names AFRISTAT directly: "La création de l'Observatoire économique et statistique d'Afrique subsaharienne (AFRISTAT), plus d'une décennie auparavant, en a été le premier signe" [The creation of AFRISTAT, more than a decade earlier, was the first sign of this]. Separately names COMESA in connection with trade-statistics harmonisation (not CPI specifically): "le Marché commun des pays de l'Afrique de l'Est et de l'Afrique australe (COMESA) avec l'harmonisation des statistiques du commerce extérieur" [COMESA, with the harmonisation of foreign trade statistics]. Also references the African Charter on Statistics's development by the AU Commission. Djibouti's own INSTAD-founding decree separately confirms accession to AFRISTAT via "Loi n°176/AN/12/6ème L" — note this law number implies a 2012 legislature session, a discrepancy against this corpus's earlier af-grok-synthesis.json history note citing a 2010 AFRISTAT accession year for Djibouti; flagged, not resolved.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational strategy document (2011-2015 planning horizon, likely superseded by a newer edition not located this round).

reports.title: Constitution de la République de Djibouti (1992)
reports.description: Djibouti's 1992 Constitution, Titre X ("Des collectivités territoriales"). Resolves this file's own earlier `_dropped` note — Grok located and this session independently re-fetched the primary text (MJP Digithèque, a French academic constitutional-text mirror, the same hosting tier already used elsewhere in this branch for constituteproject.org/WIPO Lex texts). Directly verified via curl + HTML extraction. Article 85: "Les collectivités territoriales sont créées et administrées dans les conditions définies par la loi. Ces collectivités s'administrent librement par des conseils élus et dans les conditions prévues par la loi" [Territorial collectivities are created and administered under conditions defined by law. These collectivities are freely self-administered by elected councils, under conditions provided by law]. Article 86: "Dans les collectivités territoriales, le délégué du Gouvernement a la charge des intérêts nationaux, du contrôle administratif et du respect des lois" [In the territorial collectivities, the Government's delegate is responsible for national interests, administrative oversight, and compliance with the law]. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to Grok's own paraphrase: Grok's response described these articles as stating the collectivities "enjoy administrative and financial autonomy" — that specific phrase does NOT appear anywhere in the actual French text of Article 85 or 86; the primary text establishes self-administration by elected councils, not a financial-autonomy guarantee. Grok also cited "Articles 85-87" as Titre X, but Article 87 is actually the FIRST article of Titre XI ("De la révision de la Constitution"), unrelated to territorial collectivities — a real citation error, caught by independent re-verification of the primary text rather than taken on Grok's word. No fiscal-transfer mechanism or percentage is specified anywhere in this Titre; the detailed financing regime is left entirely to ordinary law, consistent with dj-loi-174-territorial (still not independently located this round, per the dropped note below).

dependencies.basis: Djibouti's own national statistics strategy names AFRISTAT's founding as a formative event for the national statistical system: "La création de l'Observatoire économique et statistique d'Afrique subsaharienne (AFRISTAT), plus d'une décennie auparavant, en a été le premier signe." General institutional acknowledgment rather than a CPI-methodology-specific citation, so 'cites' rather than 'methodology_depends_on', matching the Guinea/Madagascar convention for support-mention-only findings. `afristat-ihpc-guide-2014` already exists in the corpus — reused per the branch's node-id discipline.

_dropped.why: SNG-WOFI (a secondary OECD/UCLG observatory) originally reported the 1992 Constitution's Titre X, Articles 85-87, establishing regions/communes with administrative/financial autonomy — the primary text was unreachable in this file's original research round (robots.txt/SSL errors). FOLLOW-UP 2026-08-13 (Grok + independent re-verification): the primary text was located and is now minted as `dj-constitution-1992` — but no edge is drawn from it to `dj-instad-cpi`, because the Constitution says nothing about statistics or CPI (it was never a plausible target for that specific edge, autonomy language or not). More importantly, the SNG-WOFI "administrative/financial autonomy" framing and Grok's matching paraphrase both turned out NOT to match the actual French text (see `dj-constitution-1992`'s own description: Article 85 establishes self-administration by elected councils only, with no financial-autonomy language, and Article 87 is not even part of Titre X — a real citation error, caught independently). Kept as `reason: 'note'` rather than 'resolved', since no edge naming this pair actually exists in the graph.

A French technical-committee document ("Comité technique Foncier et développement," not a Djiboutian government document) quotes Loi n°174/AN/02/4ème L (7 July 2002) Articles 80 and 93 on fiscal transfers to territorial collectivities ("Des dotations et transferts de l'État"; "Une dotation globale de l'État est consentie pour le fonctionnement") with specific article numbers — a real, quotable citation, but from a secondary/third-party source rather than Djibouti's own Journal Officiel text (not locatable this round). Consistent with this branch's standing practice of not minting secondary-sourced legal paraphrase as a report node (matching the earlier UNICEF Angola and NAYMOTE Liberia precedents) — recorded here as a strong lead for a future session with better access to the Journal Officiel de Djibouti. UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF/G.23): the primary text of Loi n°174/AN/02 was independently located and verbatim-verified this round via two cross-confirming legal-text mirrors (droit-afrique.com and FAO's FAOLEX database) and is now minted as `dj-loi-174-2002-decentralisation`, with live dependency edges, in the companion file dj-g23-municipal.json (this file's own dependencies array is unchanged, so `reason` here is left as `no-document` rather than `resolved` per this branch's rule that 'resolved' requires the live edge to exist in the same file's dependencies array).
